title.es-ES: Piedra bajo el nombre del prefecto

event.en: A fragmentary inscription found at Caesarea names Pontius Pilate as prefect of Judaea and records a building dedication. It is evidence for his office, not a record of the trial of Jesus.
event.es-ES: Una inscripción fragmentaria hallada en Cesarea nombra a Poncio Pilato prefecto de Judea y registra una dedicación edilicia. Acredita su cargo; no documenta el proceso de Jesús.

historicalOutcome.en: The inscription remains incomplete. Preserving its surviving words does not recover the missing text or establish unrelated events.
historicalOutcome.es-ES: La inscripción sigue incompleta. Conservar sus palabras no recupera el texto perdido ni acredita otros acontecimientos.

sourcePassages.passage: COJS entry, paragraphs describing findspot, reused block, dedication and titulature; inscription translation names Pontius Pilate as prefect of Judea.

supportedClaim.en: The Caesarea inscription attests Pilate's title and a building dedication; it does not attest the trial of Jesus.
supportedClaim.es-ES: La inscripción de Cesarea acredita el título de Pilato y una dedicación edilicia; no documenta el proceso de Jesús.

sourcePassages.limitations: Fragmentary stone reused in a stairway; COJS is a secondary catalog entry. The campaign's 27–36 range is an editorial slice of the conventional prefecture dates, not the inscription's date.
sourcePassages.reviewState: consulted by collection agent; architect interpretation and independent historical review pending

event.en: Tacitus, writing decades later, reports the execution of Christus under Tiberius by Pontius Pilate. The conventional dating around 30–33 is reconstructed. The households and refuge journey here are fictional.
event.es-ES: Tácito, décadas después, informa de la ejecución de Christus bajo Tiberio por Poncio Pilato. La fecha convencional hacia 30–33 es una reconstrucción. Los hogares y su traslado al refugio son ficticios.

historicalOutcome.en: Local success changes no documented execution and proves no ancient refuge operation. The historical account and the fictional household task remain separate.
historicalOutcome.es-ES: El éxito local no cambia la ejecución documentada ni demuestra una operación antigua de refugio. El relato histórico y la tarea doméstica ficticia siguen separados.

sourcePassages.passage: Tacitus, Annals 15.44, passage on Christus and the Neronian punishments; DCC notes distinguish Tacitus' report from other evidence and observe Christian sources do not mention an arson charge.

supportedClaim.en: Tacitus, writing decades later, says Christus was executed under Tiberius by Pontius Pilate. The passage does not place the execution in a specific year or record a refuge episode.
supportedClaim.es-ES: Tácito, décadas después, dice que Christus fue ejecutado bajo Tiberio por Poncio Pilato. El pasaje no fija un año concreto ni registra un episodio de refugio.

sourcePassages.limitations: Retrospective Roman literary testimony, not eyewitness evidence. The 30–33 date is a modern estimate; the episode candidate's 'Christian sources' wording should cite those separately if retained.
sourcePassages.reviewState: consulted by collection agent; architect interpretation and independent historical review pending

event.en: Paul describes his change of allegiance as a revelation and commission. His letter mentions Arabia and Damascus without a complete itinerary or exact year. The revelation is attributed to his account.
event.es-ES: Pablo describe su cambio como una revelación y un encargo. Su carta menciona Arabia y Damasco sin un itinerario completo ni un año exacto. La revelación se atribuye a su relato.

historicalOutcome.en: The local relay preserves a representation of Paul’s testimony. Its couriers do not establish his route through Arabia or recreate a supernatural event.
historicalOutcome.es-ES: El relevo local conserva una representación del testimonio de Pablo. Sus correos no acreditan su ruta por Arabia ni recrean un hecho sobrenatural.

sourcePassages.passage: Galatians 1:13–17: Paul recalls persecution, a divine revelation/commission, Arabia, and return to Damascus.

supportedClaim.en: Paul says he persecuted the assembly of God and describes his change as a revelation and commission; he names Arabia and Damascus but gives no complete itinerary or exact year.
supportedClaim.es-ES: Pablo dice que persiguió a la asamblea de Dios y describe su cambio como revelación y encargo; nombra Arabia y Damasco, pero no ofrece itinerario completo ni año exacto.

sourcePassages.limitations: The revelation is Paul's theological account, not an independently verifiable supernatural event. Year range c.33–36 is reconstructed; do not stage an unreported journey.
sourcePassages.reviewState: consulted by collection agent; architect interpretation and independent historical review pending

event.en: In Galatians, Paul reports visiting Jerusalem, spending fifteen days with Cephas and meeting James. His relative chronology leaves the calendar date uncertain.
event.es-ES: En Gálatas, Pablo informa de una visita a Jerusalén, quince días con Cefas y un encuentro con Santiago. Su cronología relativa deja incierta la fecha de calendario.

historicalOutcome.en: The exercise distinguishes the claims in Paul’s surviving account from fictional archival notes. It supplies no independent transcript of the meetings.
historicalOutcome.es-ES: El ejercicio distingue las afirmaciones del relato conservado de Pablo de notas archivísticas ficticias. No aporta una transcripción independiente de los encuentros.

sourcePassages.passage: Galatians 1:18–19, especially Paul's 'fifteen days' and named contacts; Yale Bible Study chronology page consulted for the broader chronology anchor (Gallio/Delphi).

supportedClaim.en: Paul reports a Jerusalem visit, a fifteen-day stay with Cephas, and seeing James.
supportedClaim.es-ES: Pablo informa de una visita a Jerusalén, una estancia de quince días con Cefas y un encuentro con Santiago.

sourcePassages.limitations: This repeats the preceding episode's source/event and should be made a distinct editorial angle or treated as duplicate. Relative interval and date of Paul's call remain uncertain; the Yale overview does not make the exact year certain.

event.en: Suetonius reports disturbances among Jews in Rome and an expulsion under Claudius, mentioning Chrestus. The identification and conventional dating around 49 remain debated. The households here are fictional.
event.es-ES: Suetonio informa de disturbios entre judíos de Roma y una expulsión bajo Claudio, y menciona a Chrestus. Su identificación y la fecha convencional hacia 49 siguen debatidas. Los hogares del escenario son ficticios.

historicalOutcome.en: The relocation illustrates a consequence of the expulsion account. It does not establish that all Roman Jews left, identify Chrestus, or prove this specific departure route.
historicalOutcome.es-ES: El traslado ilustra una consecuencia del relato de expulsión. No demuestra que todos los judíos romanos se marcharan, identifica a Chrestus ni acredita esta ruta concreta.

sourcePassages.passage: Suetonius, Claudius 25.4: Claudius expels Jews from Rome after disturbances 'impulsore Chresto'. Cambridge scholarly article search result notes scholarly disagreement in dating this incident (41 vs c.49).

supportedClaim.en: Suetonius reports disturbances among Jews in Rome and an expulsion under Claudius, mentioning 'Chrestus'.
supportedClaim.es-ES: Suetonio informa de disturbios entre judíos de Roma y una expulsión bajo Claudio, y menciona a «Chrestus».

sourcePassages.limitations: The text does not identify Chrestus with Jesus/Christ, specify a year, or show that Christians were the only people expelled. The c.49 date is conventional and debated; this candidate's Christian-conflict reading is a hypothesis.

event.en: Acts narrates a Jerusalem debate about gentile inclusion and circumcision. Paul gives a separate account of a Jerusalem visit and agreement in Galatians. The two cannot be treated as one securely identified meeting without argument.

historicalOutcome.en: The reception task changes no theological agreement. Acts and Galatians remain separately attributed accounts with a disputed relationship.

sourcePassages.passage: Acts 15:1–29: narrative of a Jerusalem meeting debating circumcision of gentile adherents and a set of requirements; compare Paul's distinct account in Galatians 2:1–10.

supportedClaim.en: Acts narrates a Jerusalem debate about gentile inclusion and circumcision; Paul independently describes a Jerusalem visit and agreement about mission in Galatians 2.
supportedClaim.es-ES: Hechos narra un debate en Jerusalén sobre la inclusión gentil y la circuncisión; Pablo describe por separado una visita y un acuerdo sobre la misión en Gálatas 2.

sourcePassages.limitations: Acts and Galatians cannot be harmonized into one securely identified meeting without argument; date c.49–50 is reconstructed. The Oxford Handbook page is an overview, not primary evidence; source selection should cite both accounts and signal disagreement.
sourcePassages.reviewState: consulted by collection agent; architect interpretation and independent historical review pending

supportedClaim.en: Paul describes another Jerusalem visit with Barnabas and Titus, a private presentation, agreement about missions and remembering the poor.
supportedClaim.es-ES: Pablo describe otra visita a Jerusalén con Bernabé y Tito, una exposición privada, un acuerdo sobre misiones y el recuerdo de los pobres.

sourcePassages.limitations: A retrospective Pauline account; no composition date is asserted. It does not independently establish that this is the same meeting narrated in Acts15 or a transcript of that meeting. Not a physical game object in c49–50.

factualIntro.en: A fragmentary inscription found at Caesarea names Pontius Pilate as prefect of Judaea and records a building dedication. It is evidence for his office, not a record of the trial of Jesus.
factualIntro.es-ES: Una inscripción fragmentaria hallada en Cesarea nombra a Poncio Pilato prefecto de Judea y registra una dedicación edilicia. Acredita su cargo; no documenta el proceso de Jesús.

personalIntro.en: I copied titles as carefully as stories. I never met that prefect, and our inherited records cannot tell me everything his name now means to you.
personalIntro.es-ES: Copié los títulos con tanto cuidado como los relatos. Nunca conocí a aquel prefecto y nuestros escritos heredados no pueden decirme todo lo que su nombre significa ahora para ti.

factualOutro.en: The inscription remains incomplete. Preserving its surviving words does not recover the missing text or establish unrelated events.
factualOutro.es-ES: La inscripción sigue incompleta. Conservar sus palabras no recupera el texto perdido ni acredita otros acontecimientos.

personalOutro.en: My first lesson in the archive was restraint: a title is a title, not proof of every story told about its owner.
personalOutro.es-ES: Mi primera lección en el archivo fue la prudencia: un título es un título, no la prueba de todas las historias contadas sobre quien lo ostenta.

factualIntro.en: Acts portrays teaching, meals and sharing within the early Jerusalem community. This is the book’s account, not an independent census or proof that every household lived alike.

personalIntro.en: My grandmother marked the meals in the margins. I used to read only the speeches. She knew a community also had to set a table.

factualOutro.en: The scenario illustrates the communal practices described in Acts. Its two kitchens, quantities and delivery rounds are playable reconstruction.

personalOutro.en: Sharing begins with attention to what each house needs. It does not make every disagreement disappear.
personalOutro.es-ES: Compartir empieza por atender a lo que necesita cada casa. No hace desaparecer todos los desacuerdos.

factualIntro.en: In Galatians, Paul reports visiting Jerusalem, spending fifteen days with Cephas and meeting James. His relative chronology leaves the calendar date uncertain.

personalIntro.en: Fifteen days: a precise memory inside an uncertain calendar. I have learned not to mistake one kind of precision for another.
personalIntro.es-ES: Quince días: un recuerdo preciso dentro de un calendario incierto. He aprendido a no confundir una clase de precisión con otra.

factualOutro.en: The exercise distinguishes the claims in Paul’s surviving account from fictional archival notes. It supplies no independent transcript of the meetings.
factualOutro.es-ES: El ejercicio distingue las afirmaciones del relato conservado de Pablo de notas archivísticas ficticias. No aporta una transcripción independiente de los encuentros.

personalOutro.en: I would rather preserve a speaker and a limit than make a tidy chronology no source can carry.
personalOutro.es-ES: Prefiero conservar una voz y un límite antes que ordenar una cronología que ninguna fuente sostiene.

personalIntro.en: My grandmother kept letters that disagreed. She would not let me scrape away the difficult lines just to make the shelf look peaceful.

personalOutro.en: A road may be safe while the words carried along it remain difficult. We need to preserve both truths.

factualIntro.en: Suetonius reports disturbances among Jews in Rome and an expulsion under Claudius, mentioning Chrestus. The identification and conventional dating around 49 remain debated. The households here are fictional.
factualIntro.es-ES: Suetonio informa de disturbios entre judíos de Roma y una expulsión bajo Claudio, y menciona a Chrestus. Su identificación y la fecha convencional hacia 49 siguen debatidas. Los hogares del escenario son ficticios.

personalIntro.en: A distant writer leaves a name we cannot securely identify. I will not turn that uncertainty into a reason to erase the people who had to leave.
personalIntro.es-ES: Un autor lejano deja un nombre que no podemos identificar con certeza. No convertiré esa incertidumbre en una razón para borrar a quienes tuvieron que marcharse.

factualOutro.en: The relocation illustrates a consequence of the expulsion account. It does not establish that all Roman Jews left, identify Chrestus, or prove this specific departure route.
factualOutro.es-ES: El traslado ilustra una consecuencia del relato de expulsión. No demuestra que todos los judíos romanos se marcharan, identifica a Chrestus ni acredita esta ruta concreta.

personalOutro.en: A household carries more than a label another person gave it. Our archive should leave room for that burden.
personalOutro.es-ES: Un hogar lleva más que la etiqueta que otra persona le puso. Nuestro archivo debe dejar espacio para esa carga.

name.es-ES: Hogares de preparación en la orilla oeste
Patio de suministros del camino occidental

text.en: Collect three luggage consignments and assemble six of the eight households alive at the supply yard.
text.es-ES: Recoge tres remesas de equipaje y reúne con vida seis de los ocho hogares en el patio de suministros.

receiptText.en: Three luggage identities and six household arrivals are required.
receiptText.es-ES: Se requieren tres identidades de equipaje y seis llegadas de hogares.

personaReaction.en: Their bundles do not tell us what Chrestus meant.
personaReaction.es-ES: Sus bultos no nos dicen qué significaba Chrestus.

text.en: Fund one onward provision of 280 food and 40 wood.
text.es-ES: Financia una provisión de salida de 280 de alimento y 40 de madera.

receiptText.en: One onward-provision receipt is registered.
receiptText.es-ES: Un único recibo de provisión de salida queda registrado.

personaReaction.en: Keep the food separate from the money promised for later.
personaReaction.es-ES: Distingue la comida de lo que se promete pagar después.

text.en: Bring at least six of the recorded households and all three luggage consignments to the north-bank departure district.
text.es-ES: Lleva al menos seis hogares registrados y las tres remesas de equipaje al barrio de salida de la orilla norte.

receiptText.en: The same households and three distinct consignments reached departure.
receiptText.es-ES: Los mismos hogares y tres remesas distintas han llegado a la salida.

personaReaction.en: The ledger records a departure, not the disappearance of a people.
personaReaction.es-ES: El registro recoge una salida, no la desaparición de un pueblo.

rationale.en: Aid supports departure without changing the expulsion claim.
rationale.es-ES: El auxilio apoya la salida sin cambiar la afirmación sobre expulsión.

rationale.en: Copies preserve fictional possessions.
rationale.es-ES: Las copias conservan pertenencias ficticias.

rationale.en: Finite repair supports land logistics.
rationale.es-ES: La reparación finita facilita la logística terrestre.

rationale.en: One trade provides bounded food.
rationale.es-ES: Un intercambio aporta alimento limitado.

rationale.en: Keeps the journey on one bank; no invented Tiber crossing.
rationale.es-ES: Mantiene el viaje en una orilla; no inventa un cruce del Tíber.

rationale.en: Two optional groups never substitute for main households.
rationale.es-ES: Dos grupos opcionales nunca sustituyen a los hogares principales.

episodeBlueprints.terrainInstructions: One-bank land itinerary toward the lower Tiber; departure is off-map travel, not a complete ship voyage. Avoid the later imperial Portus basin in a c49 scene. No forced bridge or cross-sea foot route.

routeHelp.en: Keep to the north-bank land itinerary. The final departure is a fictional off-map continuation; do not enter water to reach it.
routeHelp.es-ES: Sigue el itinerario terrestre de la orilla norte. La salida final es una continuación ficticia fuera del mapa; no entres en el agua para alcanzarla.

qaCases: same six households from staging ledger required
six families without three consignments cannot win
no Portus Claudian completed harbor assumed before its construction
no unexplained whole-city expulsion or exclusive Christian victim claim

difficultyLevers.easy: 12 workers; fully marked route; independent pickups can be completed in any order.
difficultyLevers.standard: 9 workers; geographic approach markers with local fog; plan deliveries and gathering in parallel.
difficultyLevers.hard: 6 workers; fewer initial supplies; all essential receiving zones and costs remain disclosed; no invented hostile army or secret deadline.

corridors.routePolicy: alternative surveyed land access in the same districts; exact intermediate geometry pending, never invent a crossing

dramatizationNotice.en: The gameplay participants, records, quantities and routes are fictional local reconstruction. Later writings inform the narrators; no copy of those later books is placed inside this earlier setting. Historical persons remain in attributed narration.
dramatizationNotice.es-ES: Los participantes, registros, cantidades y rutas jugables son una reconstrucción local ficticia. Los escritos posteriores informan a los narradores; sus libros no aparecen como objetos en este escenario anterior. Las personas históricas permanecen en la narración atribuida.

defeatText.en: The main delivery or survival contract is no longer achievable. Optional losses alone never cause this defeat.
defeatText.es-ES: El contrato principal de entrega o supervivencia ya no puede cumplirse. Las pérdidas opcionales por sí solas nunca causan esta derrota.

recoveryText.en: Recovery stock is protected. This design does not authorize free replacement of a lost unique person or object; restart from a save if an essential identity is irrecoverably lost.
recoveryText.es-ES: La reserva de recuperación está protegida. Este diseño no autoriza reemplazar gratis una persona u objeto únicos perdidos; vuelve a un guardado si una identidad esencial se pierde de forma irrecuperable.

factualIntro.en: Acts narrates a Jerusalem debate about gentile inclusion and circumcision. Paul gives a separate account of a Jerusalem visit and agreement in Galatians. The two cannot be treated as one securely identified meeting without argument.
factualIntro.es-ES: Hechos narra un debate en Jerusalén sobre inclusión gentil y circuncisión. Pablo ofrece por separado en Gálatas un relato de visita y acuerdo. No pueden tratarse como un encuentro identificado con certeza sin argumentarlo.

personalIntro.en: In my later archive, two accounts can sit on the same shelf without becoming the same page. These local journey notes are our reconstruction, not those later books.
personalIntro.es-ES: En mi archivo posterior, dos relatos pueden estar en el mismo estante sin convertirse en la misma página. Estas notas locales de viaje son nuestra reconstrucción, no esos libros posteriores.

factualOutro.en: The reception task changes no theological agreement. Acts and Galatians remain separately attributed accounts with a disputed relationship.
factualOutro.es-ES: La tarea de recepción no cambia ningún acuerdo teológico. Hechos y Gálatas siguen siendo relatos atribuidos por separado cuya relación se discute.

personalOutro.en: We have made room for visitors and left room for disagreement. An archive needs both kinds of space.
personalOutro.es-ES: Hemos hecho sitio para los visitantes y hemos dejado sitio para el desacuerdo. Un archivo necesita ambas clases de espacio.

text.en: Bring the four distinct fictional delegates alive to the western hosting district.
text.es-ES: Lleva con vida a los cuatro delegados ficticios distintos al barrio de acogida occidental.

receiptText.en: Four distinct arrivals are registered; no historical speaker is a controllable delegate.
receiptText.es-ES: Se registran cuatro llegadas distintas; ningún portavoz histórico es un delegado controlable.

personaReaction.en: Hospitality does not require me to supply a speech for someone who left none.
personaReaction.es-ES: La hospitalidad no me obliga a inventar un discurso para quien no dejó uno.

text.en: Provide one reception payment of 200 food and collect two separately labeled fictional delegate journey notes.
text.es-ES: Entrega un único pago de recepción de 200 de alimento y recoge dos notas ficticias de viaje de delegados etiquetadas por separado.

receiptText.en: Two fictional journey notes and one reception payment are registered. Neither note is Acts or Galatians.
receiptText.es-ES: Se registran dos notas ficticias de viaje y un pago de recepción. Ninguna nota es Hechos ni Gálatas.

personaReaction.en: Keep each account under its own name.
personaReaction.es-ES: Conserva cada relato bajo su propio nombre.

text.en: Deliver both distinct fictional journey notes to the south return station.
text.es-ES: Entrega las dos notas ficticias distintas de viaje en la estación de regreso sur.

receiptText.en: Both fictional journey notes have arrived; the mission supplies no transcript of the meeting.
receiptText.es-ES: Llegan las dos notas ficticias de viaje; la misión no aporta una transcripción de la reunión.

personaReaction.en: Leaving them separate is a decision too. It is the one the evidence asks of me.
personaReaction.es-ES: Dejarlas separadas también es una decisión. Es la que me pide la evidencia.

rationale.en: Supports visitors without buying doctrine.
rationale.es-ES: Ayuda a visitantes sin comprar doctrinas.

rationale.en: Two fictional journey labels preserve distinct gameplay identities; no future canonical text is an object.
rationale.es-ES: Dos etiquetas ficticias de viaje conservan identidades jugables distintas; ningún texto canónico posterior es un objeto.

rationale.en: Repair supports finite hospitality supplies.
rationale.es-ES: La reparación ayuda a suministros finitos de hospitalidad.

rationale.en: Finite consignment reduces travel cost.
rationale.es-ES: La remesa finita reduce el coste del viaje.

rationale.en: Shows the southern land departure.
rationale.es-ES: Señala la salida terrestre del sur.

rationale.en: Voluntary departure is distinct from exile.
rationale.es-ES: La salida voluntaria se distingue del exilio.

episodeBlueprints.terrainInstructions: Western plateau visitor activity, sacred meeting persons remain contextual. City compounds fictitious; no doctrinal conversion mechanics, no cathedral anachronism.

routeHelp.en: Host the visitors on the western plateau. Keep both account-copy identities through the southern return route.
routeHelp.es-ES: Acoge a los visitantes en la meseta occidental. Conserva ambas identidades de las copias durante el regreso por el sur.

actTransition.en: The next act follows work and letters in Mediterranean cities. Continue with The Weaver's Harbour. Jerusalem remains a place of diverse communities, not a conquered origin point.
actTransition.es-ES: El siguiente acto recorre el trabajo y las cartas de ciudades mediterráneas. Continúa con El puerto del tejedor. Jerusalén sigue siendo un lugar de comunidades diversas, no un origen conquistado.
